Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation), Lesson 211, Explanation of Verses

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Verses 1 to 3

Allah swears by the letter Sad and by the Qur'an. He swears by this Qur'an, which is full of admonition. This letter Sad is also created by Allah, and this Qur'an is also the speech of Allah. It is Allah who creates the letter Sad in the throat of man, and then this letter, together with the other letters of the alphabet which Allah has created, forms the styles of speech of the Qur'an. Yet all of mankind is incapable of producing speech like it, because the Qur'an is the word of Allah, and within it is a literary artistry that lies beyond human power. This miraculous quality of Allah's speech is present in the Qur'an, and it is also present in the other things Allah has created. This sound Sad that emerges from the throat of man comes forth through the creation of Allah, who made the human throat, from which other sounds also come forth. It is not within human power to construct any such moving, living instrument that produces sound, and this too is a miracle beyond the ordinary course of nature. Thousands of such miracles exist within their own bodies. If these people had only reflected upon the miracles present within their own selves, they would not have found it strange that Allah has sent down revelation to one of His servants and made one of His servants a bearer of a message, because there is nothing strange in revelation, just as each and every thing in the human being and the other things created by Allah is a miracle.

Sad, by the Qur'an full of admonition (38:1). "Sad. By the Qur'an full of reminder." The Qur'an contains laws, regulations, narratives, philosophy and matters of civilization, and in the same way it contains admonition and reminder. However, admonition and guidance towards Allah are greater than all other subjects. The principal purpose of the Qur'an is admonition and guidance, and indeed the other subjects also lead to Allah, in that they all renew the remembrance of Allah. The meaning of Dhu'l-Dhikr may also be "the renowned," and this too is an attribute of the Qur'an, that it is highly renowned.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 2:

﴿Nay, but those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition.﴾ (38:2) "Rather, these very people who have refused to believe are caught up in extreme pride and obstinacy."

Here in the discourse there appears a shift (idrab) and a sudden change of subject. Previously the subject was the Qur'an; now a comment has begun on the polytheists, that they are steeped in pride and arrogance and caught up in intense obstinacy and hostility. But this change of subject is only apparent, and the purpose of this apparent change is that the reader should reflect on the matter with seriousness. Here an oath is sworn by ﴿Sad, by the Qur'an full of reminder﴾ (38:1), which shows that the matter being spoken of is something very great, and for this reason God has sworn an oath upon it. After this, the pride and stubbornness of the polytheists is mentioned. The matter regarding the particle "bal" (rather, nay), whether before or after the particle of idrab (the particle "bal"), is one and the same. Their attention is drawn to how much God gives importance to the Qur'an, and how the polytheists, because of their obstinacy and stubbornness, disregard the Qur'an.

After this it is explained that, in the history of humanity, all those nations which displayed arrogance and, as a result, fell into obstinacy and stubbornness, were wiped off the face of the earth. Because they displayed enormous pride and adopted intense hostility towards the Islamic call. Just look at their condition in history: they are crying out and wailing, and no one listens. Now all that has left their minds; now they are becoming submissive and pleading. They have abandoned enmity, and now they are becoming extremely well-behaved. But at that time, when the birds have eaten the crop!

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 3:

﴿How many generations before them have We destroyed! And they cried out when there was no longer any time for escape.﴾ (38:3)

Perhaps the study of these pages of history will have an effect on them, so that they give up their arrogance and abandon their unjustified hostility, and do not place themselves on the same stance as those destroyed nations, who cried out and called for help, yet their cries were not heeded. Now they have ample time before them. They can save themselves from that cry of helplessness when there is no one to hear and no way of escape.

This was a harsh blow to shake them awake. Now it is explained in detail what their arrogance and their hostility consisted of. Listen to the details:

Verses 4 to 7

Translation: They were amazed that a warner had come to them from among themselves. The disbelievers said, "This is a sorcerer, a great liar. Has he made the many gods into one God? This is truly a strange thing." And the chiefs of the people went away saying, "Go on and remain steadfast in the worship of your gods. This matter is being said with some other purpose in mind. We have not heard of this in the latter religion. This is nothing but a fabricated tale."

That was their arrogance.

﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ (38:8) — this was the arrogance. And their hostility was:

﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ (38:5) — and this is also a cause of their hostility.

﴿We have not heard of this in the latter religion﴾ (38:7), and that ﴿This is nothing but a sorcerer, a great liar﴾ (38:4), and ﴿This is nothing but a fabricated tale﴾ (38:7). All of these were causes of their hostility.

The fact that a messenger is a human being has been a matter of wonder since ancient times. This objection has been repeated in every age since messengerships began. Messengers kept coming, and objections of this kind kept being raised.

And they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves (38:4). Yet the most fitting thing is that the warner should be one of them: a human being who knows what people think, what their feelings are, what their doubts and inner conflicts are, and what weaknesses and shortcomings exist within them. Only a human being can know where and how human beings are weak, where they feel the pressure of desires and inclinations, what the limits of their capacity and power are, how much hardship they can bear, before which obstacles and difficulties they become helpless, and what things influence them.

The Messenger is a human being; he is from among people and lives among people, so his life is an example for them. They adopt his conduct, and they regard him as their own brother, one of themselves. The human and social ties between a people and their Messenger already exist, so they can adopt the path he follows, and it can be asked of them to adopt it, because one person has already put this system into practice and demonstrated it, a person who is one of them and a human being like them.

But it is astonishing that the most reasonable and necessary matter has always been a cause of wonder to people. They have considered it unprecedented and have denied it, because these people did not understand the wisdom of sending Messengers from among humans. Nor did they understand the station of prophethood. Instead of regarding the Messenger as a human leader and guide who shows them the way of Allah, they regarded the Messenger as a strange, incomprehensible and imaginary figure. Thus they would not accept simple, ordinary human beings as Messengers. They regarded the Messenger as a figure who is imaginary, who cannot be touched, who cannot be seen, who is not manifest, and who has no practical life on this earth. In short, they wished to see the Messengers in the form of a legendary figure, and just as their own beliefs were, they wished to see the Messengers likewise.

But it was Allah's will that His final Messengership for mankind be most practical and realistic. It would contain a pure, wholesome and elevated order of life for people, and this final message would be a reality upon the earth, not based on illusions, imaginations and mere fanciful examples. It would be based on realities, not merely on illusions and myths.

And the disbelievers said, "This is a sorcerer, a great liar" (38:4). The disbelievers said this simply because they could not conceive of the messengership of one like themselves. Furthermore, they said it so that people would become averse to Muhammad (ﷺ), and so that the truth which Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, which was clear, would become doubtful in the eyes of people; since Muhammad (ﷺ) was famed for truthfulness and integrity, they did this to render him suspect in people's eyes.

The actual reality, and there is no doubt about this reality, is that the polytheists of Makkah never, at any stage, truly believed their own claim that Muhammad (ﷺ) was a sorcerer or a great liar, for they knew Muhammad (ﷺ) very well. The reality is that this was one of the crude weapons in the propaganda and misleading campaign they were running against Muhammad (ﷺ). In this way they wished to protect themselves, their status and their false beliefs, because they faced a threat from the Islamic movement; its existence threatened their hollow and false values and even the existence of their artificial customs, and the chiefs of Quraysh understood this well.

We have mentioned this point before and mention it here again: the chiefs of Quraysh began this false propaganda campaign with great seriousness and deliberation. In this way they wished to protect their existence, their customs and their ideologies. Likewise, they wished to prevent the danger that the influence of the Islamic movement would spread among the Arab tribes during the season of Hajj.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq has narrated that some elderly people gathered with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, as the season of Hajj was approaching. Al-Walid said to them: "O chiefs of Quraysh, you know that the season of Hajj is coming, and the delegations of Arabia will begin to arrive, and they have certainly heard about this man. So agree upon one view on this matter, so that you do not each say something different and end up contradicting one another." They said, "O Abd Shams, you say something, and give us a firm position so that we all say one thing." He said, "You tell me, and I will listen and then form an opinion." Someone said, "Call him a soothsayer (kahin)." Al-Walid said, "That is not right; by God, he is not a soothsayer. We have seen soothsayers, and this Qur'an is neither the murmuring of soothsayers nor their rhymed speech." Someone said, "Call him mad." He said, "He is not mad either. We know madmen well; he is not overcome by strangulation like madmen, nor is he in mental confusion, nor does he have whisperings." They said, "Then call him a poet." He said, "His speech is not poetry either. We know poetry: it is neither rajaz nor hazaj, neither qarid nor maqbud nor mabsut. So this speech is not poetry." They said, "Then call him a sorcerer." He said, "He is not a sorcerer either. We have seen sorcerers and their magic tricks; this is neither their blowing nor their knotting." They said, "Abd Shams, then you tell us what we should call him." He said, "By God, his speech has sweetness; its roots are deep and its branches bear fruit. Whatever you say of it, people will know that your statement is false. Yet the closest thing that can be said is that you call him a sorcerer, for what he brings separates a man from his brother, a man from his wife, and a man from his family, like magic." So they agreed on this one statement. During the season of Hajj they sat on the roads, and whoever passed by, they warned him, saying, "Beware, a sorcerer has appeared in this city," and they themselves would describe Muhammad (ﷺ) to people. This was the reality of what they were saying.

"A sorcerer, a great liar" (38:4): while they themselves knew that Muhammad (ﷺ) spoke the truth; he was neither a sorcerer nor a liar.

Moreover, they also wondered that he was calling people to believe in one God instead of all the gods, whereas the greatest truth is that the Lord of this universe is one.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 5:

﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ And the chiefs of the people went out saying: "Go on, and remain steadfast in the worship of your gods. This thing is surely something intended for some other purpose. We have not heard of this in the latter religion. This is nothing but a fabrication." (38:5–7, in part)

The Qur'an vividly portrays their dismay and bewilderment at the Islamic worldview.

﴿Has he made the gods into one God?﴾ (38:5), meaning: has he turned all the gods into a single God? Thus the natural Islamic belief is presented as something unthinkable and inconceivable.

﴿Indeed, this is a strange thing﴾ (38:5). The word "ʿujāb" shows that their state of alarm and bewilderment was very great.

The Qur'an also gives a powerful picture of the struggle they were waging to erase the effects of Islamic beliefs from the minds of the masses. They strove exceedingly so that the people would remain fixed upon their inherited beliefs, even though those beliefs and ideas were false and baseless. They would convince the common folk that behind this movement there was some secret hand, that they themselves were the chiefs and were aware of secret plots, and that a deep conspiracy was being carried out.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 6:

Wa-anṭalaqa... yurād (38:6): "And the chiefs of Quraysh went away saying, 'Go on, and keep steadfast in the worship of your gods. This matter is certainly being sought for some other purpose.'" This is not a matter of religion or ideology. It is some other deep conspiracy, and it is the duty of the common masses to leave this matter to the elders, who understand secret affairs well. People should remain firm in their inherited way of life and hold tightly to the beliefs of their forefathers. They should not become entangled in the conspiracy behind this modern movement. It is the job of the leaders to defend against these conspiracies. The masses should remain content. The leadership knows well the interests of the leadership, the interests of the people, and the interests of their own gods.

This is a common method of procedure, repeated in every society, by which people divert the common folk from the problems of the nation and the community. It is used by the rebellious, the insurgent, the dictators and the tyrannical forces of every society. This is because if the common people begin to think about national problems, it is a dangerous sign for the tyrannical forces; it is a threat to the authority of tyranny, since it risks the dispelling of the darkness in which the common people are drowned. The authority of tyranny is established only when the masses are immersed in ignorance.

After this, they deceive the common people through the outward belief of the People of the Book, that is, with reference to the People of the Book, although fables had entered the beliefs of the People of the Book and they had distorted the pure belief in monotheism, turning it into polytheistic beliefs. Thus they say:

In this universe there are measured things, and in them every thing is in motion. This whole universe is composed of tiny particles, whether it is a living universe or a dead one. All these particles are composed of electrons, and these electrons revolve around a nucleus composed of protons. This motion is like the motion of planets around the sun, and as a collection of countless suns, the galaxy revolves around itself. All these motions move from west to east. This is a motion contrary to the motion of time.

The elements of which the earth and other stars and planets are composed are one. All the stars are also composed of the same elements of which the earth is composed. They are all composed of particles, and particles are composed of electrons, protons and neutrons. All particles, without exception, are composed of these three components.

"Just as the whole of matter is composed of these three components, so too energy returns to one single origin. Light and heat, ultraviolet rays, radio waves, X-rays and all other rays are in reality different kinds of magneto-electric energy. Their speed is one; the difference lies only in their presence." "Matter is composed of three components, and energy is composed of waves."

"Einstein's special theory of relativity proves that matter and energy are one and the same thing. Experiments have confirmed this claim. A final experiment has also come to light, which has openly announced, and the whole world has heard, that in a modern bomb the atom took the form of energy."

"Thus it is proven that matter and energy are one thing."

This is the unity in the physical formation of this universe, and only recently has man been able to discover its reality. In the continuous motion of this universe too there is a kind of harmony and unity, as we have repeatedly pointed out. Furthermore, all the movements of this universe are orderly and continuous, so regular that not even a second's disruption occurs in them, nor is there any agitation in them. Moreover, there is such balance in the whole system that the motion of no celestial body is interrupted, nor does any collision occur between celestial bodies. And when we study the stars and planets in those galaxies that are near us, and that float in this expanse of the cosmos, it becomes clear that their orbits, their motions and their distances are fixed. No change or alteration occurs within them. Everything about them is predetermined, following a plan, that is, they move in accordance with an unchangeable plan and design.

I think this brief pause is sufficient for the study of the unity found within the system of the universe and the cosmic testimony to the belief. The belief in Tawhid is the essential truth, and the reform and progress of man is not possible on any other belief. Therefore, without clarifying the belief in Tawhid, the human conception of the universe cannot be complete. Nor can human worth and value be determined in this universe, nor can the relationship between man and this universe take the right direction. Nor can the conception of the Being who brought this universe into existence be correct in human minds, nor can the relationship between man and God be correct. Therefore, to give the human consciousness the right direction and to keep human conduct in a correct state, the explanation of the belief in Tawhid is necessary.

Now observe that the one who believes in Allah alone, who understands the meaning of this belief in Tawhid, his relationship with his Lord is also correct, and his relationship with the whole universe apart from Allah also becomes correct. And these relationships are realistic, and there is no excess or deficiency in them. Thus there is no confusion in his consciousness, and his thinking is not divided among various gods. Nor is anyone other than Allah imposed upon him.

And the one who believes in Allah and who considers Allah the source and origin of this universe deals with this universe, and with the things within it, with mutual acquaintance, love and affection, and his life is full of hope, and his life is shaped in a form that is very different from the person who does not believe in Allah the Exalted. And he does not find himself in harmony with his environment and his society.

The one who believes in Allah receives specific guidance from Allah so that he may shape his life in accordance with the natural order found within this universe and with the Shariah revealed by Allah. The law of Allah operates upon the universe as well, and the Shariah established by Allah prevails over human life, and thus man's practical life becomes harmonious with this universe.

In short, the perception of this truth is necessary so that human consciousness is correct. It should be illuminated, it should have the right direction, and it should be harmonious, balanced and coordinated with the universe spread around it. And the relations of man among themselves, his relations with this universe and his relations with his society should be clear and defined. Whether these relations are moral or concern conduct, whether they concern collective affairs, whether they are personal or human.

This is why the Qur'an gives such importance to Tawhid, and the struggle for the belief in Tawhid has been carried out by all the prophets who came from Adam (peace be upon him) onward. And all the messengers have insisted strongly upon the belief in Tawhid. The words of the declaration of Tawhid have also remained one, and its meaning has also remained one.

In the Qur'an, so much emphasis has been placed upon the belief in Tawhid that it has been repeated again and again. Insistence has been placed upon it. The issue of Tawhid and its requirements has been explained again and again through various styles. Especially in the Meccan surahs there is much emphasis upon it, while in the Medinan surahs too the belief in Tawhid has been emphasized according to Medinan themes, where the aspect of sovereignty and the right of legislation is more prominent. These were the reasons why the polytheists of Makkah were astonished that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rejected all the gods and believed in only one God. Therefore they argued with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over this, were astonished, turned people away from this belief, and had gathered all their resources against this way of life.

Now, the second aspect of their astonishment: they did not consider Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) worthy of the office of prophethood from the standpoint of wealth and personal eminence. They thought that a leader should be some khan or nawab.

ما سمعنا... اختلاق (38:7): "We have not heard of this in the latest religion. This is nothing but a fabrication."

The unbelievers of Quraysh were alluding to the spread of the doctrine of the Trinity among the Christians at the time the Qur'an was revealed, and to the belief in the divinity of Uzayr (ʿUzayr) that had spread among the Jews. The leaders of Quraysh were pointing to this and saying: "We have not heard of this in the latest religion. Neither Judaism nor Christianity contains this pure monotheism. Therefore, what Muhammad (ﷺ) is presenting is a fabricated religion of his own." Islam struggled greatly to establish pure monotheism, and through the doctrine of tawhid it removed every kind of human deviation, hidden shirk (shirk khafi), manifest shirk (shirk jali), and all other forms of misguidance and crooked thinking. This is because the doctrine of tawhid is the truth upon which this entire universe is founded, and the entire universe bears witness to it in a most clear manner. Furthermore, the reform of human personality, of one's inner self, of one's principles of life, and of the subsidiary matters of life cannot take place until a person is firmly established upon the doctrine of tawhid. It is appropriate here to give a detailed account of how intensely the Quraysh were resisting the doctrine of tawhid, how greatly they were terrified by this belief, and how strange and unfamiliar they considered the belief in the One God amid countless deities. It should also be explained how, throughout human history before the Quraysh, all polytheists consistently opposed this belief, and how, from Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) onward, all the Prophets consistently insisted upon this belief and made tireless efforts so that people would accept it and so that it would truly take root in their minds. First of all, it is appropriate that readers understand the importance of the doctrine of tawhid.

The reality is that the doctrine of tawhid is the fundamental truth upon which this entire universe rests, and the entire universe bears clear witness to the unity of divinity (wahdat al-uluhiyyah). The laws of nature that apply on this earth are, in their reality and essence, completely a unity, and they show that the will under which these laws came into existence is one single will. By taking an overall view of this universe, or by studying a single part of this universe, it becomes well known that unity is found within it, and this unity shows that the will which brought it into existence is one.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 8:

Verse No. 8 (1)

This was not a matter for wonder, but the leaders of Quraysh were afflicted with envy. Because of this envy they would resort to arrogance, enmity and malice. Ibn Ishaq narrates from Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri that once Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and Akhnas ibn Shariq ibn Amr ibn Wahb al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, went out at night to listen to the Qur'an. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite the Qur'an in prayer at night. Each of these three, unaware of the others, sat down in his own place. They kept listening until late in the night. When the dawn appeared, they set out for their homes. On the way they happened to meet one another, and they reproached each other severely. They said to one another, "Do not do this again. If some foolish people see you, they will be affected by it in their hearts." They departed. When the second night came, each of them again returned and sat in his designated place. They listened until late at night. When dawn broke, they set out and, on the road, again came together and reproached one another for the previous night. Then they left. On the third night, each of them again came and sat down. They listened through the night. When dawn came, they began to leave, and on the road they again saw one another. Now they said, "We will not go until we make a covenant." So they made a formal agreement and then departed. In the morning, Akhnas ibn Shariq took his staff and went first to Abu Sufyan. He said, "Abu Hanzala, tell me what you heard from Muhammad. What is your opinion about it?" He replied, "I heard some things which I recognise and understand the meaning of, and some things which I did not hear and do not understand the meaning of." Akhnas said, "By God, my situation is the same." After this, he came to Abu Jahl, met him at his house, and said, "Abu al-Hakam, what is your opinion about what you heard from Muhammad?" He replied, "What did I hear? We and the Banu Abd Manaf have always been in competition. They provided food, and we also provided food. They gave mounts to people, and we also gave mounts. They gave gifts, and we also gave gifts. In war too we competed, until we were like racehorses running side by side. Now they say, 'A prophet has arisen among us, and revelation comes to him from the heavens.' How can we produce a prophet to match that? By God, we will never believe in him, nor will we ever affirm him." Akhnas then stood up and left him to his own state.

Look, this is open malice, which is why Abu Jahl does not acknowledge the truth, even though, having listened to the words of Allah for three consecutive nights, he knew that it was true. It was envy and malice that stood as an obstacle in the way of his faith, and this is the secret behind the matter.

﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ (38:8). "Has the Qur'an been revealed to this man among us, when there were others?" These were the very people who used to say it. ﴿Why was not this Qur'an revealed to some great man of the two towns?﴾ (43:31). By "the two towns" they meant Makkah and Ta'if, where the chiefs of Quraysh held authority and where their religious leadership and direction were established. Moreover, they had also heard that a new prophet was about to come, and when Allah bestowed this office upon Muhammad (ﷺ), these people burned with jealousy and thought that they themselves deserved this great mercy of Allah and this exalted rank, and not him. Was Muhammad (ﷺ) alone worthy of it out of all the world? Allah answers them in the same manner, with contempt, in which there are indications of threat and warning.

Verse No. 8 (2)

Their question was: "Was this person alone chosen from among us to receive the revelation of the Qur'an?" Yet they themselves were doubtful about the truth of the Qur'an. There was no certainty in their hearts that this Qur'an was from Allah. They were in severe uncertainty about the very reality of revelation, yet despite this they also acknowledged that this Qur'an was a lofty speech in comparison with ordinary speech. Now the address turns away from their statement about the Qur'an, and their uncertainty is set aside. They are threatened with a severe punishment.

﴿But they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾ (38:8). That is, they say these things only because they have not tasted My punishment; Allah has granted them deliverance through His kindness. But when the punishment seizes them, they will no longer speak such words. At that time they will fully know the reality of their situation.

Now comes the final comment: these people consider the favour and grace bestowed upon Muhammad (ﷺ) to be greater than his deserving, so the question is put to them: are they the ones in charge of distributing the mercy of the Lord, having the authority to show mercy to whomever they will and to withhold it from whomever they will?

Verse 9

This is a severe rebuke to them, for their words are a plain act of impudence in the presence of the Glorious Majesty. They are meddling in matters in which they have no right to interfere. It is for Allah alone to bestow His grace upon whom He wills and to withhold His bounty from whom He wills. He is the Almighty, the Possessor of all powers; no one can stand as an obstacle before His will. He is the Giver, the Generous, and there is no limit to His bounty. These people are scowling and displeased that Muhammad (ﷺ) has been made a Messenger. Is the distribution of Allah's gracious favours in their hands? Are the treasures of Allah in their charge?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 10:

Verse 10 (1)

They have no answer to this, because they cannot make this claim. For their own belief was that the owner of the heavens and the earth is Allah, that it is He who gives and He who withholds, that He bestows His bounties and He alone grants what is fitting. And since sovereignty over the heavens, the earth and what lies between them is not in their hands, they should not interfere in the affairs of Allah, the Supreme Sovereign, for He alone has absolute disposal. Now, by way of mockery and to silence them, they are told: suppose their answer is in the affirmative, that they are the supreme sovereigns over the heavens, the earth and what lies between them, then let them put their sovereign power to use.

Verse 10 (2)

So that their control over the heavens, the earth and the stages between them becomes evident, and that they carry out Allah's affairs themselves, distribute Allah's treasures, giving to whom they wish and withholding from whom they wish. Since their conduct demands this, for they raise objections to the distribution of prophethood. That was the mockery. Now, what is their fate, and what end are these people going to face?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 11:

Verse 11

Their end is nothing but that they will be thrown far off and their army will be routed. It is a place far from the position they claim for themselves, where their army is destined to be defeated. This army has no share in the dominion of Allah. It cannot alter the decrees of Allah, and it has no standing before the will of Allah. It is an army of unknown lineage, of unknown standing, and it is defeated. As if defeat is its inseparable attribute, a part of its very identity. And this army is made up of various factions, whose inclinations differ and whose desires differ.

The enemies of Allah and of the Messenger of Allah can only advance to the extent that the Holy Quran depicts them with the colours of weakness, helplessness and frailty. It gives the impression that these people are very far from the sphere of Allah's control and management, even though in the eyes of the world they may be tyrannical and mighty, their grip may be harsh, and their word may prevail in the world for some time. The Quran depicts such tyrants in this manner throughout the whole of human history.

﴿Jundun ma hunalika mahzumun min al-ahzab﴾ (38:11): "This is but a small host of the confederates, destined to be routed right there."

This is the example of those who passed in history before the Quraysh: the people of Noah, the people of 'Ad, Pharaoh of the great pyramids, which are like pegs upon the earth, the people of Thamud, the people of Lut, and the people of Shu'ayb, who are also called Ashab al-Aykah, that is, the people of the dense thickets. These are the confederates who denied the messengers. So see what their end was. Though they were mighty and possessors of stakes, ﴿It was then that My punishment was justly due upon them﴾ (38:14). What was to happen, happened. They were so utterly destroyed that no trace of them remained.

Such was the position of those who passed in the past. As for these people, a punishment awaits them. This will come before the Day of Reckoning, and there will be one cry, and then nothing will remain in the whole world.

Verse 15

This means that when that time comes, there will be no delay in it even as long as the interval between the two milkings of a she-camel. This is because the milk of a milch animal is extracted at its appointed time, and no advancing or delaying is done in it. This Ummah is the last Ummah, and Allah has given it time and respite until the Day of Resurrection, because Allah does not destroy this Ummah utterly as He destroyed the earlier nations.

It is a great mercy of Allah that He has granted this Ummah a long respite. But it is regrettable that the people of Quraysh did not regard this as a blessing, did not give thanks to Allah for it. Instead, they kept demanding that the appointed punishment of their own end come quickly, and they kept praying, "O Allah, whichever of us has the evil end, let him reach it quickly," and that this punishment come upon them in this world even before the Day of Reckoning.

Here, the Qur'an concludes its discussion about them and turns its address towards the Prophet (ﷺ). He is consoled that he should not care about their foolishness. By demanding punishment, they are committing impropriety (sū' adab) in the presence of Allah. In reality, they do not even believe in the establishment of the Day of Resurrection. They are ungrateful for Allah's mercy. The Prophet (ﷺ) is directed to read the circumstances of the earlier prophets, and the trials that came upon them, and that after this, Allah's mercies descended upon them.

Lesson No. 212: Explanation of the Verses

This entire lesson consists of stories and the exalted examples of the lives of the Messengers. These examples are being presented before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he may reflect upon the lives of the earlier Messengers, while the Quraysh were denying him, making accusations, charging him with falsehood, and regarding his prophethood as something unprecedented. He should be patient over this and endure the hardships that often make a person's heart grieve.

All these narratives, for the consolation of the Messenger ﷺ, present incidents of Allah's mercies and kindnesses upon the Messengers: what bounties Allah bestowed upon them. Some Messengers were granted authority and great kingdoms, and great favours were conferred upon them. These events are related because the people of Quraysh were astonished that Muhammad ﷺ had been granted the office of prophethood. Yet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not the first Messenger. Great kingdoms had been bestowed upon the Messengers. For some, even mountains were subjected to them, and birds would join them in glorifying Allah. For some, the winds were subjected, and jinn and devils were also under their command, such as Dawud and Sulayman (peace be upon them both). After all, is it any matter of wonder that Muhammad, son of Abdullah, was selected for the office of the final age (akhir al-zaman)?

These narratives also establish that Allah constantly watches over His Messengers. At every turn of their lives, at every moment, guidance is given to them, and they are made to undergo experiences. They too were human beings, just as Muhammad ﷺ is a human being. These Messengers also had human weaknesses. Therefore, Allah, by constant watchfulness, protected them from human weaknesses. Allah continually shows them the correct position, guides them, and tests them so that He may forgive their lapses. The purpose of mentioning these matters is to give comfort to the heart of the Messenger ﷺ: that he is working under the watch of his Lord, and at every step Allah is watching over and supporting him.

Verses 17 to 20

Isbir (ٱصْبِرْ): be patient. This is the important characteristic of the life of all the Messengers, the quality on account of which all of them are counted as one group. All of them walked the same path, all of them bore hardships, all of them were tested, and all of them were patient. Patience was the provision of all of them. Within the chain of the prophets, all of them endured difficulties in graded measure. Their lives were a trial, and trial was filled with tests and afflictions. They were patient over calamities, and these were a test for them; and then they were also patient over Allah's grace and bounty, and this too was a trial. In both conditions patience is necessary, and they were patient.

If we keep in view all that the Qur'an narrates of the lives of the Messengers, then patience itself is the foundation of their lives and the important feature of their lives. Their whole life consists of trials, hardships, struggle, and perseverance and steadfastness.

From the study of the lives of the prophets it becomes clear that it is a chosen life composed of trials. Indeed, it is a life of hardship. It is an open book, in which only the songs of trials and patience are written, and perfect examples have been presented for humanity, so that history may record how the human spirit overcomes hardships and the desire for the necessities and comforts of life, and how the human spirit rises above all those values in which the world takes pride, and how the human spirit becomes detached from the deceptive things of the world and the things the self desires. It becomes entirely for Allah, and thus it attains success through trials. It gives preference to Allah over everything other than Allah. Only on reaching this station can it then challenge humanity and say: this is the way of life, this is the path of dignity, and this is the way that leads, at its highest heights, to Allah.

Isbir 'ala ma yaqulun (38:17): "Be patient over what they say." And what were the things they used to say?

Aj'alal-alihata ilahan wahidan (38:5): "Has he made the gods into one God?" And this is what they used to say.

A-unzila 'alayhi al-dhikru (38:8): "Was the Reminder sent down upon him from among us?" and so on. Allah turns His Prophet's attention to this: simply continue to be patient. The Prophet ﷺ is guided to live, in contrast to the models of these disbelievers, with other models: sincere and noble-natured models. These models are those of his brother Prophets who came before. Their examples are presented before him so that he may feel a close bond with them, that they are his brothers, his kin and relatives. Accordingly, the Messenger ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on my brother so-and-so..." and "I am the nearest of people to that Prophet."

Isbir 'ala... awwab (38:17): "O Prophet, be patient over what these people fabricate, and recount before them the story of Our servant Dawud, who possessed great strength and always turned to Allah in every matter." It is said of Dawud (peace be upon him) that he was a man of great strength, yet in every matter he turned to Allah. Earlier, the peoples of Noah, 'Ad, Pharaoh, Thamud, the people of Lot and the Companions of the Thicket (Aykah) were mentioned. All these nations were extremely rebellious. They displayed their strength by oppressing people, transgressing, and denying the truth. In contrast, Dawud (peace be upon him) was also a man of great strength, but he was awwab: in every matter he turned to Allah, obedient to Allah, worshipful, and remembering Him, even though he was a man of strength and sovereign power.

The early part of the story of Dawud and his distinguished performance in the army of Talut have already been described. After the time of Musa (peace be upon him), this army of the Children of Israel rose under the leadership of Talut. In that era the Children of Israel were in decline, and they had demanded that a king and a ruler of the state be appointed for them by Allah. This army clashed with Jalut (Goliath), the tyrannical enemy of the Children of Israel. Dawud killed Jalut. In that period Dawud was a young man. Thus his star shone, and eventually he became king. But his conduct remained that he always turned to Allah in every matter. He was obedient and worshipful, and was always engaged in remembrance and seeking forgiveness.

Along with this authority and sovereignty, Allah also granted him prophethood, and He gave him a most beautiful voice. He would praise Allah with the sweetest melody, and he was so absorbed in remembrance and recited praise and glorification with such devotion that all the veils between him and this universe were lifted. Thus mountains and birds would also glorify Allah with him and extol and magnify the Lord. The mountains would hum along with him, and the birds would flutter around him, and all of them were praisers of their Generous Lord.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verses 18–19:

"We made the mountains subservient to him, glorifying (Allah) with him at evening and at sunrise, and the birds gathered together; all of them turned to him in repentance."

Ordinary people who read this verse will be astonished at how inanimate mountains could glorify Allah along with Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him), and that they did so morning and evening, especially when he went into seclusion to remember his Lord. There they would sing the praises of Allah with exceptional melodiousness, and would extol and glorify Him. The birds would gather on hearing their songs, and would also repeat them. Truly, this will be astonishing to people, because it runs contrary to customary matters and familiar patterns. When people are accustomed to something, they do not feel such things. How did this kinship come into being between the species of humans and birds and the solid mountains?

However, there is nothing astonishing in this. It is not a surprising claim. The fact is that the reality and essence of all creatures is one, although in form, appearance, kind and category they differ from one another. All these things are one in relation to their Creator, and they are parts of a single comprehensive existence, whether they are living beings or non-living things. When a person becomes sincere for his Lord and attains the stage of purity of the inner self and illumination, all these veils of kind and category are lifted, and all these things come before him with their true reality. All this creation becomes one behind these outward veils. Different kinds, categories, forms and shapes, outward colours and characteristics are in fact veils; the reality lies behind them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verses 21:

Verses 21 to 24

The explanation of this incident is that Hadrat Dawud (peace be upon him) would devote a portion of his time to the affairs of the state, judging between people. For some time he would devote himself to seclusion, worship, glorification and praise, and reciting the hymns of praise of Allah. When he secluded himself in the mihrab (the prayer niche), no one was permitted to enter until he himself came out.

One day it happened that two persons climbed over the wall and entered this place of seclusion. He was alarmed by their entering in this manner, because no believer or responsible person could enter his place of seclusion like this. So these two persons also sensed his fear and hastened to try to reassure him.

The sign of the chapter's narration is clear here, so I'll translate the passage as it stands.

Qutb's commentary on Surah 38, verse 22:

"They said: 'Do not be afraid. We are two disputing parties, one of whom has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path.'" (38:22)

Therefore, they have come to seek a decision. "Judge between us with the truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path." (38:22) After this, one of them began to state his claim.

"Indeed, this is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes, and I have only one ewe. Yet he said, 'Entrust it to me,' and he overpowered me in speech."

Akfilnee means "give it to me," "put it under my ownership," and "entrust it to my care"; 'azzanee means "he prevailed over me."

As far as the case itself is concerned, the claim as stated shows that this is an act of oppression which admits of no justification. Accordingly, Prophet Dawud (عليه السلام) began to pass judgment even before hearing the reply to the claim, because on the face of it the brother's conduct appeared oppressive. Therefore Dawud did not even speak to the other party: he neither heard his response to the claim nor asked him for any explanation, but simply passed judgment upon hearing the claim.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 24:

Qāla laqad... mā hum (38:24): "Dawud replied: By demanding that he add your ewes to his ewes, this man has certainly wronged you. And indeed, most of those who live in partnership wrong one another. Only those who believe and do righteous deeds are spared from this, and such people are few." (﴿Qāla laqad ẓalamaka bisu'āli naʿjatika ilā niʿājihī wa inna kathīran minal-khulaṭāʾi la-yabghī baʿḍuhum ʿalā baʿḍin illā alladhīna āmanū wa ʿamilūṣ-ṣāliḥāti wa qalīlun mā hum﴾)

Khulaṭāʾ (partners, associates) refers to relatives and those who frequently associate with one another. From the context it appears that these two persons disappeared at this point, because they were angels who had come to test him; that is, the test was intended for that Prophet whom Allah had made the ruler, leader and judge of the common people, and had commanded to judge among people with justice, and to investigate cases thoroughly before pronouncing judgment. The test becomes more severe when a case is presented before them in which, on the surface, clear injustice appears; yet it is the attitude of a judge that he should not be swayed by the words of either party, should not decide in haste, and should not rule merely on apparent statements or circumstances. In contrast to the statement of claim, he should demand the response of the defendant, because sometimes hearing the response changes the very nature of the claim, and it becomes evident that although the statement of claim appears correct outwardly, the real nature of the matter is different, or that the plaintiff is concealing some facts and deceiving. At this point it occurred to Dawud (ʿalayhis-salām) that this matter was not a genuine case but an examination paper.

Wa ẓanna Dawūdu annamā fatannāh (38:24): "Now Dawud became certain that We had in truth tested him." Here his true disposition comes to the fore: he was one who turned to Allah in every matter.

Fa-istaghfara rabbahū wa kharra rākiʿan wa anāb (38:24), As-sajdah: "So he asked his Lord for forgiveness, fell down prostrating, and turned in repentance." (﴿Fa-istaghfara rabbahū wa kharra rākiʿan wa anāb﴾)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 25:

Verse 25

Some tafsir works, under this verse, have brought in material from Israelite narratives (Isra'iliyyat) and have gone very far in the matter of the trial of Prophet Dawud (David). They have related things that are not even fitting for prophethood; indeed, they cannot be reconciled with the office of prophethood at all. Some narrations, although they tried to explain away certain people's actions in order to reduce the severity of the wrong involved, have also gathered within themselves some legendary elements. Therefore these narrations are not worthy of being related or of being given consideration, because they are entirely contrary to the Qur'an's own comment on this matter.

﴿وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾ (38:25) "Indeed, for him with Us is a near station and a good place of return."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 26:

The commentary that has come on this story makes it clear what the nature of Prophet Dawud's trial was. Allah had given Dawud rule so that he would judge among the people with justice, and therefore it became settled that the trial and test concerned judicial proceedings. Thus it was said:

Verse 26

To Dawud (peace be upon him) it was said that sovereign authority over the earth had been given to you, so that you judge among the people with truth, and that in these judgments you do not give consideration to your own desires. As for the Prophet, he is protected from following the desires of the self. The meaning is that you should not decide on the basis of your initial inclination. It should not be that you decide without thinking and without investigation, for judgments made hastily, without inquiry, are in this way mistaken. At the end of the verse there is a general command, for all those who go astray from the path of Allah, who forget Allah. The result is that on the Day of Judgment they will suffer a severe punishment.

After the principle of walking in truth in the earthly caliphate has been established, and after the rulings on judging people with truth and justice, and before the story of Dawud (peace be upon him) ends, this truth is joined to the universal truth upon which the heavens and the earth stand, and upon which the whole cosmos subsists between the heavens and the earths. This truth is very deep within this cosmos, and is much more general than merely the truth of the caliphate on earth and the truth of justice among people. This truth is broader than this earth, extending beyond even the life of this world to the world of the Hereafter. Just as this cosmos is encompassed by it, so too the world of the Hereafter is encompassed by it. On this universal truth this final messengership is based, and this final Book of Allah is the manifestation and interpreter of that all-encompassing and comprehensive truth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verses 27–29:

The passage from verses 27 to 29

This is the real point. In these three verses the great truth is stated, and the Qur'an gives it great importance. It is a most profound, comprehensive and magnificent truth. Its roots and branches run deep and spread far through this whole universe. The truth is that the heavens and the earth, and whatever lies between them, are not a plaything. They were not false, they are not false, and they will not be false. Rather, it is the Truth. This universe stands upon realities. From this all-encompassing truth all other truths blossom, and this truth is in fact the reality and nature of this universe and then of this earth. Truth in human rule over this world, truth in establishing justice and fairness among people, truth in the consciousness of people, and truth in the establishment of their deeds are the branches of this great Truth and reality.

Therefore, those who believe and have truth in their consciousness, and who do righteous deeds and whose conduct is correct, cannot be like the corrupters (mufsidin). Therefore, on this earth, the weight of the righteous and the weight of the wicked and dissolute cannot be equal. This is the great truth which this Book has brought, so that people may ponder over its verses and that those of them who are people of understanding may take admonition from it. It is that great truth. And people should obtain a generous share of this great reality and reflect upon it. The disbelievers, in reality, do not even conceive of this great truth, because their nature and their consciousness are deprived of that great truth upon which this universe stands, and of which the Qur'an is the bearer. The disbelievers indeed harbour ill thoughts about their Lord, and they are deprived of perceiving this great truth.

﴿That is the assumption of those who disbelieved; so woe to those who disbelieve, from the Fire﴾ (38:27).

The Islamic Shari'ah is in fact an explanation of this great truth of Allah upon which this whole universe stands. The justice and truth which Allah demands from rulers and caliphs in this world is a part of this universal truth and reality. The demand of this truth is that just as it is established in the universe, so it should be established in the system and society of human beings, so that this great truth is not incomplete, but all its aspects are established. Therefore, those who deviate from the Shari'ah and deviate from justice actually deviate from the truth upon which this entire universe stands. In this way they create a great disorder and corruption in this universe. Thus a clash arises among the cosmic forces, and therefore in such a case there is a danger of clash among the cosmic forces as well as among human forces. Thus there is a danger of breakdown both in the universe and in human society. For a tyrant, a rebel, and one who clashes with the sanctity of Allah and the Shari'ah of Allah cannot remain sound and upon the straight path. And even if this weak and feeble human being rebels, what can he do to harm the great powers of Allah? If he creates disorder and causes harm, he will do so to himself. Against the mighty and overpowering forces of Allah, he will be helpless.

This is the great reality upon which all people of wisdom should reflect, and men of understanding and intellect should take admonition from it. In the midst of this narrative, this instructive event is related and commented upon so that this important matter may be made clear. Further favours of Allah upon Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him) are enumerated: by His grace, Allah produced from his descendants a person of perfection such as Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him), upon whom Allah bestowed great favour. Indeed, many kinds of bounties were bestowed. The trial of Sulayman...

After the accounts of Allah's favours upon him, there is mention of the events of the outpouring of Allah's mercies.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verses 36–38:

﴿Then We made the wind subservient to him, flowing gently by his command wherever he willed, and the devils—every builder and diver, and others bound in chains.﴾

Subjecting the wind to one of Allah's servants by His command does not mean that it has gone out of Allah's will. Despite human subjugation, the wind continues to blow under the Divine will. By Allah's command, it blows gently in accordance with its nature. When Allah makes it easy for one of His servants that his action becomes an expression of the Divine will, and the servant's command becomes in accordance with the command of Allah, then the cosmic forces are seen moving along with the command of Allah and along with the command of the servant. Then these winds blow very gently wherever that servant wishes. This is an action whose occurrence is not independent of Allah. It occurs in forms of action. For example, Allah Almighty addresses the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and says:

﴿If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and those who spread false rumours in Madinah do not desist, We will surely set you upon them. Then they will not remain your neighbours in it except for a little.﴾ (33:60)

What is its meaning? The meaning is that if they do not desist, Allah will set in motion His will in the form of the will of Muhammad (ﷺ), and by raising you against them He will thus expel them from Madinah. As a result of Allah's will, Muhammad (ﷺ) will begin fighting against them. Thus there will be harmony between the will of Allah and the will of the Prophet (ﷺ). Both wills will merge, and the will of Allah will be seen in the form of the measures taken by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah Almighty had subjected the wind to Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him) in the same sense as Sulayman wished. Likewise Allah would have subjected the winds, or Sulayman's will would have aligned with whatever way Allah willed.

Likewise, the devils were also subjected to him, and he got construction work done from them. In the sea and on land these people dived for him, and brought out whatever things Sulayman wished. And Allah had granted him full power to punish opponents and corrupters. He was given full authority to apprehend, imprison and seize criminals. There was no problem of peace and security in his kingdom; that is, criminals, individually or collectively, would be arrested and put in chains.

He was given full authority over the distribution of wealth in the earth: he could give to whomever he wished and withhold from whomever he wished, or give to each as much as he wished.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verses 41:

Verses 41 to 44

The patience of Prophet Ayyub (peace be upon him) has become a proverb and is very well known. "Sabr-e-Ayyubi" (the patience of Ayyub) is an idiom. However, a layer of Isra'iliyyat (narrations of Israelite origin) has accumulated over this story, and the reality has been lost in superstitions. The true reality is as the Qur'an clarifies: Prophet Ayyub (peace be upon him) was a righteous servant who turned to Allah. A trial from Allah came upon him, and in it he showed excellent patience. It also appears that his trial was such that his wealth went away, his health went away, and his wife also left him. But in all these life-threatening afflictions, he held firmly to the hand of the Lord, the Exalted. His trust in Allah remained, and he remained content with the will of Allah.

Shaytan kept casting whisperings into the hearts of those people who were few in number but remained attached to him, and among them was his wife. Shaytan would put these whisperings into their hearts, saying that if Ayyub were a chosen servant of Allah, then Allah would never have put him into this trial. When these people related these words to Prophet Ayyub, the pain these Satanic whisperings caused him was even greater than the physical and material calamity. When his wife said such things before him, he took an oath that if Allah freed him from this affliction and he became healthy, he would flog his wife. Some have said that he would flog her one hundred lashes.

When, upon these trials, harassment from Shaytan also began, and its effect started to reach his sincere followers, and it affected his own heart, then he called out with a supplication:

﴿Indi massaniya ash-shaytanu bi-nusbin wa 'adhab﴾ (38:41), meaning: "Indeed, Shaytan has afflicted me with hardship and torment."

When it became clear that he was truthful and patient, and that he also hated the whispering suggestions of Satan, and that these were only increasing his suffering, then God's mercy now envelops him. The days of trial pass, and his health returns. The Lord, the Exalted, commands him to strike his foot upon the ground. Cool water will emerge, from which he may drink and bathe, and his health will be restored.

﴿Strike with your foot. This is a cool bath and a drink﴾ (38:43) "Your foot upon the earth: here is cool water to wash in and to drink." Further mercies come in this manner.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 43:

"And We gave him back his family, and as a mercy from Us, and a reminder for people of understanding, We gave him the like of them with them." (38:43)

Some narrations state that God restored to life those of his children who had died, and gave him an equal number of children in addition. The Qur'an does not explicitly state that the dead were brought back to life. It may also mean that those who had left him and gone away, together with their households, were returned to him, and then further offspring were granted as additional bounty, as mercy and as indulgence. These favours were bestowed so that people of intellect might take a lesson from them.

The purpose of all these stories is that whoever among God's servants remains patient in trials, God shows him kindness, and in the end mercy is bestowed upon him.

As for the outcome of their oath: God's mercy enveloped him and his wife, because his wife had served Prophet Ayyub (peace be upon him) greatly during that long trial, and she too had shown great steadfastness. God had commanded that he take as many twigs as the number of lashes he had sworn to strike, and strike her once with all of them together. In this way his oath would be fulfilled and he would not be in breach of it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verse 44:

"And take in your hand a bundle of grass and strike with it, and do not break your oath" (38:44). This concession was granted to him because, in that great trial, he remained patient in accordance with Allah's will, stayed as an obedient servant, and in the end turned to Allah alone in supplication.

"Indeed, We found him patient. How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was ever turning back (to Allah)" (38:44).

These three narratives have been mentioned in some detail. The purpose was to show that Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions should be patient with the difficulties they face. Now a reference is made to a group of messengers. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 38, verse 45:

Verses 45 to 48

Surely they were among Our chosen and righteous servants, and they were before Solomon. However, we do not have definite information about the era of Prophet Ayyub (Job). Nor is there accurate information about Dhul-Kifl. The Qur'an has been content with only allusions about them. The name of one of the prophets from among the Children of Israel is "Al-Yasha'" in Hebrew, which in Arabic is "Al-Yasa'". For this reason we also prefer this. As for Dhul-Kifl, there is not much historical information about him.

"Ulil-aydi wal-absar" (38:45): "people of great strength and far-sighted vision." The meaning is that they were people who performed righteous deeds with their hands and feet, and who, in terms of their beliefs, held upright thought. It is as if one who does not perform righteous deeds is weak, and one who does not have sound thought is blind despite having eyes.

In the Qur'an, in describing the distinguishing quality of these prophets, it is said that they were purely devoted servants of Allah. Their second special quality was that they constantly remembered the Hereafter and took it into account. They worked only for the pleasure of Allah and for success.

Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home (of the Hereafter). (38:46)

They were chosen on account of a particular quality, and that quality was the remembrance of the Abode of the Hereafter. Their rank and their elevation are what made them chosen.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 38, verses 47–48:

﴿And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen and excellent.﴾ (38:47)

Moreover, Allah makes it explicit and commands Muhammad (ﷺ) that you should remain in the spiritual company of these prophets. Remember their patience and perseverance, and hope for the grace and favour that ultimately came upon them. Bear patiently the denial of your people and the harm that you are suffering because of it, for the way of all the noble messengers has been patience and perseverance. And after the messengers, the way of all the callers to faith has also been patience, and it is always so that Allah shows mercy and compassion to His patient servants. He grants them strength and authority, and He sends down upon them mercy and blessings. The reward and the outcome that Allah has for His servants is, in every case, better. Before the mercy of Allah and the blessings of Allah, the plots of schemers and the deceptions of deceivers have no worth at all. Allah is always the Guardian of His servants.

Lesson No. 213: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 49 to 64

In the previous lesson we were in the company of the chosen servants of Allah. The subject under discussion was the trial of their lives and the prominent aspect of their patience in the face of hardships. After the trial, all these servants were enveloped by Allah's mercy and His grace. The purpose of that gathering of remembrance was to show us that this is the highest kind of life on this earth, and that this temporary life should be spent in this manner. Now, in this lesson, it is explained what the condition of the God-fearing servants will be in the Hereafter, and what the days and nights of the rebellious and the deniers will be. Thus, in the previous lesson the subject was the transient life of this world, and in this one the days and nights of the everlasting life are under discussion. This life is shown here in the form of scenes, as is the style of the Noble Qur'an. It is appropriate here that I give some extracts from my book "Mashahid al-Qiyamah" (Scenes of the Resurrection).

These scenes begin with two scenes and two ends, which stand in complete contrast to one another. Taken as a whole they are opposed to each other, and in their parts too they are mutually contrasted. In form, meaning and characteristics, the two stand facing each other. The righteous (muslihin) have reached a good end (husn ma'ab), whereas the corrupters (mufsidin) have reached an evil end (shar ma'ab). For the God-fearing (muttaqin) there are gardens whose doors are open for them at all times:

﴿Gardens of Eden, their doors thrown open for them﴾ (38:50). In them they recline, facing one another, and good food and good drink are available to them. With them are maidens of modest gaze, of equal age. Though young, they are modest; they neither lift their gaze to anyone nor walk about with airs. Moreover, all these provisions are everlasting, and they come from Allah, and ﴿they have no end﴾ ("ma lahu min nafad", they are not to be exhausted). Thus the deniers too are seen in a place of rest, and it is a most wretched place of rest.

This is the Qur'anic commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on Surah 38, verses 86–88:

Verses 86 to 88

This is indeed a call to specific salvation. Its outcome has been made clear, and it has also been warned against most strongly. This is such a sincere call that the caller seeks no reward or recompense. This caller is sound in nature. He speaks in the language of ordinary people. There is no affectation or artificiality in his speech. He says only those things which the logic of fitrah (natural disposition) teaches him, and which are easy to understand. And this is a reminder for those who, because of their heedlessness, have forgotten this admonition and advice. And this is that great news and headline whose consequences they will soon see with their own eyes, but after a very short while. This is a worldwide news for the whole earth. In truth, within a few years of this verse, those people did see its consequences. And on the Day of Resurrection too they will see its consequences, when Hell will be filled with humans and jinn.

Lamala'anna jahannama minka wa-mimman tabi'aka minhum ajma'in (38:85): "I will surely fill Hell with you and with all those among them who follow you."

This is the conclusion of this surah, and it is in harmony with the opening discourse of this surah and with its themes and issues, which have been discussed in it. This is a final and profound blow, and through it, it has been declared what the future holds for this movement of Islamic revolution.

Wa-la-ta'lamunna naba'ahu ba'da hin (38:88): "After a little while you will certainly come to know its news."

Sadaqa Allahu al-'Azim.
